_readme: STD-028 file-size ratchet. Enforced when `[loc] required = true` in appcheck.toml
and `loc` is part of `make check`, so a regression REFUSES the gate instead of
printing a warning nobody reads. The check names every offending file.
A WORKLIST, not an exemption: an entry may LEAVE this file, never join it, and
no frozen number here may rise. Lower it in the same commit that shrinks the file.
TWO UNITS (ADR-0110). `files` is physical code lines, the unit every role's CAP
is stated in. `substance` is substance TOKENS for converted Python entries, and
that is the governed number for them: a layout collapse refunds one to four
tokens against the dozens a real addition costs, so returning to a frozen token
count means removing substance. A converted entry's `files` value is informational.
An entry with no `substance` value keeps the line rule.
GROWTH IS REFUSED, and a substantive change must LEAVE the file smaller. A change
that alters an entry's substance (not comments, docstrings or layout) and ends at
its frozen token count is refused as HELD: adding thirty tokens and deleting thirty
elsewhere is not burn-down. This is ADR-0098's Option 2, armed by ADR-0110.
NOTHING ELSE ENFORCES BURN-DOWN. An untouched entry may sit here forever and no gate
will object: this file records debt, it does not schedule its repair. No age,
expiry or deadline logic exists. Measured 2026-08-31: 619 of 630 fleet entries sit
above their cap, 293,092 excess code lines frozen as legal.
FIX BY EXTRACTING a cohesive block into its own module; `appcheck closures <file>`
lists the blocks that can leave without creating an import cycle. Do NOT collapse
lines. Returning to the frozen number is not the goal; the cap is.
BURN DOWN:   appcheck baseline loc <project> --apply
Lowers numbers, drops resolved entries, and records substance values for
Python entries that lack them. Refuses to freeze anything new.
Re-generating at an UNCHANGED cap is baseline-stuffing and is the recorded
anti-goal of this workstream. It is legitimate exactly twice, and --apply now
requires you to say which -- in the command, not only in the commit message:
--adoption-event   enforcement is being armed for this project for the first time
--cap-changed      max_lines itself changed, so the set must be re-frozen
KNOWN LIMIT: keys are paths and there is no relocation allowance. RENAMING OR
MOVING a baselined file reads as new debt. Re-key that one entry in the same
commit as the move; do not regenerate the whole file.
